title: An agent's re-route of a failed job onto another lane relaunches it unrefused
body:
## Summary
The kernel refuses an agent's re-route of a failed or interrupted job when it steers on the same lane, but relaunches it unrefused when the target is on another lane.

## Description
packages/kernel/src/job.ts:359 (rerouteIn) refuses `requeue && actor.kind !== "operator"` - only an operator puts a failed or interrupted job back in a queue, the same rule retry (job.ts:316) and ackLane (job-queue.ts:112) hold. packages/kernel/src/records/reroute.ts:151 relaunchIn cancels the failed job and enqueues its successor with no actor rule, and moveRouteIn (reroute.ts:189) picks relaunch whenever the target's lane or producer differs (reroute.ts:107). Measured this round: a real failed research job (seat.text) re-routed by `{ kind: "agent" }` to the Gemini option (cloud.google) through the real port's reroute receipt + confirm answered ok - a new queued job. The MCP door's gt_job reroute (app/_server/mcp/tools/job.ts) refuses only live jobs, so a dry failed job is requeued by an agent through this door. Fixed: relaunchIn (or moveRouteIn) applies rerouteIn's actor rule when the job being replaced is failed or interrupted; then the fixture's reroute (app/(studio)/projects/_port/fixtureActs.ts reroute) takes `by` and refuses the same, as retry and ackLane now do (66e5d3b5).

## Flow
- compose + launch a film on a temp kernel, drive research to failed
- real.reroute({jobId, option: <other lane>}, agent) -> receipt; confirm with its token as agent
- observed: ok, job cancelled and successor queued; same act as a steer would be refused

## Expected impact
An agent can no longer requeue a failed job by choosing a route on another lane; the operator's retry/ack boundary holds for every requeue. Could break: an agent workflow that relied on re-routing failed dry jobs (none in tests).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one actor rule across the kernel's requeue doors
Before: agent requeue of a failed job: steer refused, relaunch ok (1 of 2 doors guarded) - reproduced on the real port this round
After: predicted 2 of 2 guarded
Method: probe - reproduced through the real port in tests/next-server/produce-fixture-parity.test.ts (case dropped before commit); the fix lives in packages/kernel, outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
packages/kernel/src/job.ts:359  if (requeue && actor.kind !== "operator") throw new AppError("refused", ...)
packages/kernel/src/records/reroute.ts:151  export function relaunchIn(t, input, actor)  (no actor check)
packages/kernel/src/records/reroute.ts:107  ... ? "steer" : "relaunch"
probe: agent confirm of research (seat.text -> cloud.google) on a failed job -> "ok"
instrument: packages/kernel/test records reroute case: agent moveRouteIn on a failed job to another lane -> refused (red today); then a produce-fixture-parity case 'an agent's re-route of a failed job back into a queue' on both sides

title: The projects page reads every job to count the Floor runs still open
body:
## Summary
/projects calls listJobs - the full jobs view - only to count Floor runs that are not done.

## Description
app/(studio)/projects/page.tsx:301-302: `const jobs = port.listJobs(); const floorRuns = jobs.ok ? jobs.value.filter((j) => j.projectId === undefined && j.state !== "done").length : 0;`. On the real side listJobs is realRead.jobsView: up to JOBS_CAP=500 job records parsed, each served (a project and parts load or a runs row read), priced, its events queried and the lanes scheduled (app/(studio)/projects/_port/realRead.ts:137) - all for one integer. The count wants `SELECT count(*) FROM jobs j JOIN runs r ON r.job_id = j.id WHERE j.state != 'done'` (or the kernel's own run index), exposed as a ServerProduce read beside listJobs (port.ts ServerProduce, both sides). Also: a failed listJobs silently draws 0.

## Flow
- open /projects on a store with N jobs
- page.tsx -> serverProduce().listJobs() -> jobsView(r, now) over min(N, 500) jobs
- fix: a `floorRunsOpen()` read on both sides (fixture: count over u.jobs of kind run not done), page uses it

## Expected impact
Every /projects load stops paying a full jobs view; the count is the same. Could break: the count's definition must match the filter (run jobs only, not done; cancelled counts as open today).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - /projects load
Before: 1 jobsView per load (<=500 jobs: parse + serve + price + events + schedule)
After: predicted 0 jobsView, 1 count query
Method: simulation - walked page.tsx and realRead.jobsView; the instrument is the passthrough jobsView counter 46016c88 added to produce-real.test.ts, pointed at the page test
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: tests/next-server/projects-page.test.ts extended with the realRead.jobsView passthrough counter over the real port: jobsView calls per page render 1 -> 0, floorRuns unchanged on a seeded store

title: The fixture's lane line is ordered by schedule, the kernel's by queue order
body:
## Summary
A fixture move swaps a job with its neighbour in scheduled-start order; the kernel swaps in (ord, n) order.

## Description
app/(studio)/projects/_port/fixtureActs.ts moveJob sorts the lane's waiting jobs by `placed.get(...).s` then `order`; the kernel's move (packages/kernel/src/job-queue.ts:139-146) and the real port's pre-read (app/(studio)/projects/_port/real.ts moveJob, `ORDER BY ord, n`) use the queue order alone. Where a waiting job is blocked or waits on an upstream, its scheduled start is later than its queue place, so `[`/`]` on the fixture passes a different neighbour than on the real side, and the toast names a different job.

## Flow
- fixture: two queued jobs on one lane, the earlier-ordered one blocked behind a failed upstream
- moveJob(later-ordered, earlier) on the fixture -> swaps by start time
- the kernel would swap by order

## Expected impact
The fixture's Runs `[`/`]` names the neighbour the real side would. Could break: tests/live/produce.live.spec.ts only matches /behind|ahead of|end of the lane queue/.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - fixture/real parity
Before: unmeasured: the fixture seeds no blocked waiting pair on one lane
After: predicted: same neighbour on both sides
Method: simulation - read both orderings; a parity case needs a seeded blocked pair on the fixture and a planned pair on the real side
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
app/(studio)/projects/_port/fixtureActs.ts moveJob: .sort((a, b) => at(a) - at(b) || a.order - b.order)
app/(studio)/projects/_port/real.ts moveJob: SELECT id FROM jobs WHERE lane = ? AND state IN ('queued', 'planned') ORDER BY ord, n
instrument: produce-fixture-parity case: a fixture project launched with a blocked upstream so two queued jobs on one lane differ in start and order; moveJob names the (ord)-neighbour

title: A fixture re-route confirm checks its token before the lane's hold
body:
## Summary
On a job its lane holds for, a stale re-route token answers the fresh receipt on the fixture and a refusal on the real side.

## Description
app/(studio)/projects/_port/realReroute.ts confirmReroute (inside one tx) checks the hold (`laneHold(t, lane)?.jobId === job.id` -> refused 'acknowledge the hold first') BEFORE comparing the token; app/(studio)/projects/_port/fixtureActs.ts reroute compares the token first (stale) and checks the hold after. The seeded interrupted Suno run holds box.chrome, so the fixture's Runs `O` on it with a moved queue shows a fresh receipt where the real side refuses.

## Flow
- fixture: the seeded interrupted job:run:run-seed-suno (box.chrome held)
- reroute receipt, then any act that moves the queue, then confirm with the old token
- fixture -> stale receipt; real -> refused, hold first

## Expected impact
The hold is the first thing the operator is told on both sides. Could break: nothing pinned on the order today.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - fixture/real parity
Before: unmeasured on the real side (needs a held lane: produce-real's crash harness)
After: predicted: refused on both
Method: simulation - read both orders; the real case needs runJob crash + recover as produce-real.test.ts does
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
app/(studio)/projects/_port/realReroute.ts confirmReroute: if (laneHold(t, again.job.lane)?.jobId === again.job.id) throw ...; if (again.receipt.token !== token) return stale
app/(studio)/projects/_port/fixtureActs.ts reroute: if (token !== receipt.token) return stale; const held = holdNames(u, job) ...
instrument: produce-fixture-parity case using produce-real's crash harness (runJob crash + recover) for a held real job: stale-token confirm -> refused on both
